name: Table
blurb: Rows of data with a header, sized by the row density token.
mechanism: A real `<table>` with `<thead>` and `<tbody>`, so column headers are announced with every cell and a screen reader can navigate it as a grid. Rows pad from `--row-px` / `--row-py`, the same rhythm menus and sidebars use. Sortable headers are `<button>`s inside `<th>` carrying `aria-sort`.
caveats: A table used for layout is worse than a div; if the data is not tabular, this is the wrong element.
Zebra striping helps scanning and hurts contrast: the striped rows here stay above 4.5:1, but check yours if you re-tint them.
On narrow screens the container scrolls sideways. That is the honest fallback - collapsing a table into cards loses the column relationship.
